question_text: How do you wire an Open-Loop Comparator, and what happens to the output?
answer_text: The output snaps completely to the positive or negative supply rail depending on which input pin has the higher voltage.
explanation_text: With no feedback resistors, an op-amp has massive open-loop gain. If the (+) pin is even slightly higher than the (-) pin, the output multiplies that difference and hits the positive maximum.
bonus_question_text: Why are dedicated comparator ICs often preferred over using standard op-amps as comparators?
bonus_answer_text: Standard op-amps recover very slowly when their outputs are pushed to the rails (saturation). Dedicated comparators are designed to switch instantly between digital logic levels.
